findings.evidence: grep -n 'lint-dot-notation' scripts/lean_source.py → lines 10, 779, 789, 792, 802, 805, 811, 823, 827; `cat scripts/lint-dot-notation.py` is 8 lines, body `from lean_source import main`.
findings.fix: Keep `main`, `read_baseline` (748), `write_baseline` (766), and `Finding` (148) in `scripts/lint-dot-notation.py`; import the parser from `lean_source` there. `lint-dot-notation.py` then holds the CLI it is named for instead of being a `from lean_source import main` shim.
findings.issue: The generic module owns the lint's CLI: `main` defaults to `scripts/lint-dot-notation-baseline.txt` (line 779), errors and reports with `lint-dot-notation: ...` prefixes (789, 792, 805, 811, 823, 827), and prints the dot-notation remediation text. A shared parser module should not name or drive one specific lint.

findings.evidence: grep -n '^ORGANISATIONAL\|^NOTATION_RECEIVERS\|^SPECIAL_NOTATION\|^def find_violations' scripts/lean_source.py → 29, 56, 115, 642; only `find_violations`/`own_declaration_paths` consume those tables.
findings.fix: Move the tables and lint logic back into `scripts/lint-dot-notation.py` and trim `lean_source.py` (and its docstring) to the command-level parser plus `qualified_declarations`. `mathlib_namespaces` (425) may stay if the follow-up check needs it.
findings.issue: Dot-notation lint policy is embedded in the generic module: `ORGANISATIONAL` (29), `NOTATION_RECEIVERS` (56), `SPECIAL_NOTATION_RECEIVERS` (115), `own_declaration_paths` (513), `find_violations` (642), and the module docstring's baseline/grandfathering paragraph (lines 5-11). None of this is reusable by the #3616 follow-up check; only `strip_comments_and_strings`, `declarations`, `scopes`, `variable_bindings`, `update_scope`, and `qualified_declarations` are.

findings.evidence: scripts/test_lint_dot_notation.py:2 docstring vs line 12 `import lean_source as lint`; .github/workflows/ci.yml:62 runs only `python3 scripts/test_lint_dot_notation.py`.
findings.fix: After the split, keep lint tests (including the `lint.main` cases at lines 395-433) in `test_lint_dot_notation.py` importing the lint script, and put parser-level tests in a new `scripts/test_lean_source.py`; add it to the ci.yml Python test list alongside line 62.
findings.issue: The test module still documents itself as "Regression tests for ``scripts/lint-dot-notation.py``" but now imports `lean_source` and exercises the shared parser as well as the lint, so parser tests are filed under the CLI script's test name.

summary: The extraction went the wrong way: the entire dot-notation lint (policy tables, Finding, find_violations, baseline I/O, and a CLI main that hard-codes the lint's name and baseline path) now lives in the generic scripts/lean_source.py, while scripts/lint-dot-notation.py is an eight-line forwarding shim. Lint-specific material must not masquerade as reusable parser infrastructure.
